decision.title: A Schematron conformance suite of sxml's own (packet )
decision.summary: sxml has its own Schematron conformance suite, tests/schematron/, for ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, with neutral expected results, recorded readings, a SchXslt cross-check and an independent check of the 2025 cases.

item.p: What: tests/schematron/, 332 cases in 18 test sets for ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, in a catalog format of its own (namespace urn:sxml:schematron-test-suite, golden file third_party/qt4tests), with catalog.xsd, coverage.xml (139 requirements of clauses 3 to 7 and the normative annexes, 131 with cases, 8 with the reason none can test them) and a README. Every schema, instance and expected result was written for the suite; the standard's text is cited by clause only.

Expected results are neutral: a multiset of findings (kind, subject as fn:path, id, role, flag, severity, subordinate document, message after whitespace normalization, diagnostics and properties), the set of raised flags, optional XPath assertions over SVRL; or schema-error, error (6.1's third outcome) or implementation-defined, each with its clause. No sxml API or error code appears. since="2025" marks the 67 cases that need fourth-edition constructs; query-binding and feature dependencies mark what a processor may lack.

Readings taken (the README lists them): whole-token parameter references; Annex B's param-names-match only for abstract patterns that declare parameters (read literally it fails every third-edition instance); one definition per variable name over schema, phase, pattern and rule, pattern variables scoped to the pattern; the subject as message context (6.3); value-of through fn:string() (several items are an error); relative rule contexts under the xpath bindings implementation-defined (the orchestrator's direction), as is how the default xslt binding is read when a result depends on it.

Cross-check: the 265 cases with since="2020" ran through SchXslt 1.10.1 on a release build of sxml (tools/crosscheck.py, report in tools/schxslt-crosscheck.txt): 198 agree, 5 implementation-defined, 13 need a binding SchXslt lacks (xslt, xpath*), 49 disagree, each with the clause that decides it (27 unchecked static errors; SchXslt's global pattern variables, shadowing, name path as a value, rule context for messages, prefix placeholders, no placeholders in subject, no base URI fixup, empty phases, joined value-of, and three SVRL omissions). The 67 2025-only cases wait for the independent check.

Against : two points differ from the standard as the suite reads it: value-of as xsl:value-of joins several items, where Annexes H to N define it with fn:string() (value-of-several-items); any schematronEdition is accepted (, 8b), where 5.5.15 requires 2025 (edition-other-value). Reading no queryBinding and xslt as 4.0 is 's choice; the suite keeps those cases dependent on the xslt binding or implementation-defined.

Existing suites: schematron/schematron-conformance (49 cases, 2016 edition, no licence: not reused), SchXslt's unit tests (MIT, not reused), XQS's BaseX tests (Apache-2.0, not reused); none covers the 2025 edition.

Addendum (2026-10-28): the independent check of the 67 2025-only cases. A separate agent derived each result from the standard alone, on copies with result and description removed; it never saw the suite, or and ran no implementation. 52 identical; the other 15 agree in substance (fired-rule listings against flags and assert-svrl, @n against @Q{}n, the conditional findings of the five optional-binding cases, let-as-mismatch an error either way, visit-each-atomic's uncompared location, edition-reported at user option). No case changed.

Addendum (2026-10-28): the edge-case pass. 182 cases more (514 in 18 sets; 104 since="2020", 78 since="2025"), each construct varied by cardinality, order, static and dynamic errors, namespaces, text (non-ASCII, astral, combining, whitespace-only, mixed), node kinds and interaction with phases, group, documents, from, visit-each, subject, abstract patterns and extends; the README's "Edge cases" table marks each pair covered, implementation-defined or not applicable (22 reasons). New readings, in the README's "Ambiguities in the standard": dynamic role/flag/severity that are empty, several or not names, static role and severity that are not names, role="$undefined" (5.4.7 against Annex J), parameters in role and severity (6.2), subject and rule variables under visit-each, the context of diagnostics and properties with a subject, subjects selecting none or several, overlapping and attribute from, later when under #ANY, duplicate documents and rule-context items, two ns for one prefix, a library as the schema, active naming an abstract pattern, whitespace in queryBinding and schematronEdition: all implementation-defined. Normative readings: include and extends-href cycles are schema errors (6.2), visit-each duplicates are evaluated twice, a role from an attribute node is its string value, syntax errors in unused abstract rules and inactive phases still make the schema incorrect (7.2). Every case on the xslt3 binding now declares the dependency (485 cases): only the default binding is mandatory (6.5). crosscheck.py collapses only 5.3's four whitespace characters. SchXslt cross-check of the 369 2020 cases: 281 agree, 55 disagree (6 new, each by the clauses already recorded: Annex A, 7.2, 6.3, Annexes H and J), 18 implementation-defined, 15 need a binding SchXslt lacks. The 78 new 2025-only cases wait for the independent check.

Addendum (2026-10-28, the orchestrator): the independent check of the 78 new 2025-only cases. The same separate agent derived each from the standard alone, on copies without results or descriptions, and without this record, or the suite. 39 identical; 39 agree in substance: 21 the suite calls implementation-defined and the check flags AMBIGUOUS (dynamic role, flag and severity that are empty, several or not names; errors in when and from; overlapping or attribute from results; visit-each with variables and subject; schema parameters; a library as schema), 6 dynamic errors on both sides (the check notes that 6.1's result "error" and D.2's svrl:error fit no finding), 1 on the optional xquery31 binding with the same conditional findings, and notation (fired-rule listings, @n against @Q{}n, no location for atomic visit-each items). One judgement call: edition-whitespace stays implementation-defined, because 5.3's stripping is a "should"; the check read Annex A's xsd:token as deciding it. No case changed. Both rounds together: all 145 2025-only cases checked. Packet done.
